title: The Choice You Cannot Undo
fact_notes: 人物・具体的な出来事は架空の思考実験・教材例。実在の調査・統計を示すものではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: Imagine that a traveler must choose between two unfamiliar towns for a weekend visit.
sentences.ja: 旅行者が週末に訪れる見知らぬ二つの町から一つを選ぶと想像してみよう。

sentences.en: Both destinations offer attractive activities, and the available information provides no decisive reason to favor either one.
sentences.ja: どちらも魅力的な活動があり、入手できる情報には一方を選ぶ決定的な理由がない。

sentences.en: The traveler makes a reservation in the first town and begins preparing for the journey.
sentences.ja: 旅行者は最初の町を予約し、旅の準備を始める。

sentences.en: However, after paying, she continues searching for photographs and reviews of the other destination.
sentences.ja: しかし支払い後ももう一方の目的地の写真や口コミを調べ続ける。

sentences.en: Each new photograph makes the alternative seem more appealing than it did before.
sentences.ja: 新たな写真を見るたびに別の選択肢が以前より魅力的に見える。

sentences.en: She notices that she is comparing the ordinary details of her actual plan with the most exciting possibilities of the rejected option.
sentences.ja: 実際の計画の日常的な細部と、選ばなかった案の最も魅力的な可能性を比較していると気づく。

sentences.en: This comparison ignores the inconveniences that might also have accompanied the alternative journey.
sentences.ja: この比較は別の旅にも伴ったかもしれない不便さを無視している。

sentences.en: It also overlooks the enjoyable experiences that she has not yet discovered in the town she selected.
sentences.ja: 選んだ町でまだ発見していない楽しい体験も見落としている。

sentences.en: A friend suggests distinguishing useful information from information that merely encourages further doubt.
sentences.ja: 友人は役立つ情報と単にさらなる疑いを促す情報を区別するよう提案する。

sentences.en: For example, a warning about a closed railway line could still help the traveler adjust her plan.
sentences.ja: 例えば鉄道路線の運休についての警告は計画の調整に役立ち得る。

sentences.en: By contrast, an attractive picture of another town may provide little practical benefit after the reservation becomes final.
sentences.ja: 対照的に予約が確定した後、別の町の魅力的な写真は実用的な利益が少ないかもしれない。

sentences.en: The traveler decides to devote her remaining preparation time to exploring the opportunities available at her chosen destination.
sentences.ja: 残りの準備時間を選んだ目的地で可能な活動の調査に充てると決める。

sentences.en: This decision does not require her to pretend that her original choice was perfect.
sentences.ja: この決定は最初の選択が完璧だったと装うことを求めない。

sentences.en: If genuinely important new evidence appears, reconsidering the arrangement could still be reasonable.
sentences.ja: 本当に重要な新しい証拠が現れたら取り決めの見直しはなお合理的になり得る。

sentences.en: But endlessly imagining an ideal alternative may prevent her from engaging fully with the experience she actually has.
sentences.ja: しかし理想の別案を果てしなく想像すると実際の体験に十分関われなくなるかもしれない。

sentences.en: Her objective changes from proving that she made the best choice to making good use of the choice she made.
sentences.ja: 目的は最善の選択をしたと証明することから、した選択を生かすことに変わる。

sentences.en: The example illustrates a difference between evaluating a decision and learning to live with its consequences.
sentences.ja: この例は決定を評価することとその結果を受け入れて暮らすことの違いを示す。

sentences.en: Careful reflection can reveal mistakes worth correcting on future occasions.
sentences.ja: 慎重な振り返りは今後修正すべき誤りを明らかにし得る。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, reflection becomes less productive when it depends entirely on an imaginary version of what might have happened.
sentences.ja: それでも、起きたかもしれないことの架空の姿だけに依存すると振り返りは生産性が下がる。

sentences.en: A reasonable decision can remain reasonable even when its outcome is not everything a person hoped for.
sentences.ja: 合理的な決定は結果が期待したすべてでなくても合理的であり得る。

vocabulary.definition: behave as though something were true
in a real or sincere way
a result someone aims to achieve
makes something clear through an example

questions.prompt: Why was the original choice difficult?
options: Neither destination had a decisive advantage.
questions.explanation_ja: 決定的な差がなかった。

questions.prompt: What did she continue doing after paying?
options: Looking at information about the other town.
Writing reviews of her actual visit.
She had checked every inconvenience equally.
She already knew the outcome of both trips.
She compared ordinary reality with an especially attractive imagined alternative.
questions.explanation_ja: 実際の普通の面と理想化された別案を比較した。

options: Undiscovered enjoyable experiences in her chosen town.
The existence of the second town.
questions.explanation_ja: 選んだ町で未発見の楽しみ。

options: A random photograph of another town.
A list of rejected hotel colors.
A warning about a closed railway line.
An advertisement unrelated to either town.
questions.explanation_ja: 運休情報は計画調整に役立つ。

options: To focus on opportunities she could actually use.
To prove no other destinations exist.
To avoid all information about travel.
To make every future decision irreversible.
questions.explanation_ja: 実際の選択を生かすため。

questions.prompt: When might reconsidering still be reasonable?
options: Whenever a different photograph looks attractive.
questions.explanation_ja: 重要な新証拠が出る場合。

options: Demonstrating that the other town is worthless.
Finding a perfect alternative in imagination.
Making good use of the decision rather than proving it optimal.
All regret proves a choice was irrational.
Reflect on choices while avoiding endless comparison with idealized alternatives.
The best decision guarantees a perfect outcome.
questions.explanation_ja: 振り返りと理想化された別案への執着を区別する。

grammar.focus: no decisive reason to favor either one
the most exciting possibilities of the rejected option
grammar.explanation_ja: 過去分詞rejectedがoptionを修飾する。

grammar.focus: even when its outcome is not everything
grammar.explanation_ja: even whenは不利な条件でも成立することを示す。

paraphrases.source: Both destinations offer attractive activities, and the available information provides no decisive reason to favor either one.
paraphrases.rewrite: The two places seem appealing, with no clear evidence that one is preferable.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 一方を選ぶ明確な根拠がない。

paraphrases.source: She notices that she is comparing the ordinary details of her actual plan with the most exciting possibilities of the rejected option.
paraphrases.rewrite: She realizes she is comparing the everyday reality of her plan with the most appealing imagined version of the other choice.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 現実と理想化された別案を比較する。

paraphrases.source: By contrast, an attractive picture of another town may provide little practical benefit after the reservation becomes final.
paraphrases.rewrite: Once the booking is fixed, an appealing image of another place may offer little actual help.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 確定後の情報は役立たない場合がある。

paraphrases.source: A reasonable decision can remain reasonable even when its outcome is not everything a person hoped for.
paraphrases.rewrite: A sensible choice can still be sensible if its result falls short of someone's hopes.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 期待以下でも合理的な決定であり得る。

discourse.role_ja: 予約後も調べ続ける逆接。
実用性の低い情報との対比。
振り返りの価値と限界。

cloze.explanation_ja: 別案の不便さを考慮しない。
